doc.title: Johnny Varro interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clearwater Beach, Florida, March 16, 2001

title: Teenage wedding jobs
summary: Wedding jobs at twelve to fifteen dollars a night with small groups, as a proving ground.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: Right. But you were still, what, still in your teens?
I was, yeah, about that time I might have been about seventeen, eighteen.
Yeah. Well that was all right.
Not too bad, yeah. And what would the band consist of? A quartet and so forth?
Trumpet, a tenor player, usually clarinet, tenor, maybe no bass. Guitar probably, drums and piano. Small groups. And we played the typical wedding songs and the “Miami Beach Rumba.”
Yeah. Well those can be good proving grounds because you’ve got to learn to do just about everything.
Well yeah. Oh listen it was good, great, you know. Some of the players were good. Some of them were pretty bad too. But you learn too. You grew that way.
